summary: _4._ The 2nd respondent then filed a fresh petition No.168/MP/2017 before the CERC, New Delhi, seeking quashing of the said letter dated 24.05.2017 of CTU with further directions to CTU to grant connectivity in terms of Commission’s previous order dated 21.09.2012. Vide order dated _6._ It was argued by the learned counsel for the appellant that the delay in filing the review petition was not deliberate and occasioned on account of the situation beyond control of the appellant. He submitted that the appellant had never entered appearance before the Commission in the petition No.168/MP/2017 and expected the CTU i.e. 3 rd Respondent PGCIL to espouse its cause also before the Commission. He pointed out that the appellant gained knowledge about the order dated 29.01.2018 of the Commission on 07.02.2018 when its copy was received from 3 rd Respondent and it came to be known from the perusal of the order that it has been passed against both, the 3 rd respondent as well as the appellant. He further submitted that the appellant requested the 3 rd respondent PGCIL to approach the Commission by seeking review of the said order dated 29.01.2018 and upon refusal of PGCIL to do so, the Board of Directors of the appellant met in the 1 st week of March 2018 to chalk out further strategy. Legal opinion was sought by the appellant and it was advised to file review petition for which the Board of Directors of the appellant again met in the last week of March 2018 and decided to file review petition. He further argued that as per the advice of the lawyer, certified copy of the order dated 29.01.2018 was applied for and the same was obtained from the Registry of the Commission on 26.04.2018, and thereafter the review petition was filed. He argued that the delay in filing the review petition was caused only for the reason that the appellant expected the 3 rd respondent to seek review of the said order dated 29.01.2018 of the Commission and further due to multiple hierarchical levels of involvement of various departments of the appellant in taking decision against the said order, engaging a lawyer, obtaining certified copy of the order to be reviewed and drafting/ filing of review petition. It is his submission that no malafide or inaction can be attributed to the appellant in these circumstances and the appellant had made out a sufficient cause for condonation of delay. He further argued that the Commission has committed a grave error in refusing to condone the delay in filing the review petition and therefore the impugned order is liable to be set aside. _7._ Per contra, the learned counsels appearing for 2 nd and 3 rd Respondents would support the impugned order submitting that it does not suffer from any error or infirmity. It is submitted that the appellant itself has been negligent in defending the petition before the CERC as it never appeared before the Commission on any date and even after coming to know about the Commission’s impugned order dated 29.01.2018, did not take any immediate steps for assailing the same and instead chose to ride on the back of the 3 rd Respondent by expecting it to seek review of the said order. It is argued that the appellant has taken inordinately long time in filing the review petition and has miserably failed to make out any cogent ground which prevented it to file the review petition within stipulated period of 45 days in terms of Regulation 103 of CERC (Conduct of Business Regulations), 1999. It is further argued that the appellant cannot claim a preferential treatment merely for the reason that it is a government body and cannot claim condonation of delay in filing the review petition mechanically in the absence of any plausible and acceptable explanation for the same. In this regard, reliance is placed upon the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in _State of Madhya Pradesh and Others versus Berulal_ SLP (C) No.9217 of 2020 decided on 15.10.2020. _8._ We have gone through the impugned order and have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties. _9._ Admittedly, there has been a delay of 53 days in filing the petition for review of the order dated 29.01.2018 by the appellant before the CERC, New Delhi. It is also admitted position that there was no representation on behalf the appellant before the Commission on 29.01.2018 when the said order was passed and the appellant gained knowledge of the same on 07.02.2018 upon receipt of a copy of the said order from 3 rd respondent. It is further manifest that immediately thereafter, appellant sent letter dated 12.02.2018 to 3 rd Respondent asking it to seek a review of the said order dated 29.01.2018 and upon refusal of the 3 rd respondent to do so, it initiated steps for assailing the said order by convening a meeting of its Board of Directors and by seeking legal opinion thereafter. It is further to be noticed that subsequent to the refusal by 3 rd Respondent to seek review of Commission’s order dated 29.01.2018, the Appellant approached its Board initially for filing appeal against the said order and in pursuance to the legal opinion received thereafter, again approached the Board for filing a review petition and thereafter initiated process for the same. In these circumstances and considering the actions initiated by the appellant upon gaining knowledge of the order dated 29.01.2018 of the Commission, as noted hereinabove, it is difficult to say that the appellant remained negligent and was not diligent in commencing process for assailing the said order. _13._ In the light of above discussion, the impugned order of the Commission cannot be sustained in the eyes of law. The same is hereby set aside. The Appeal is allowed and the delay in filing the review petition stands condoned.
title: WEST BENGAL STATE ELECTRICITY TRANSMISSION COMPANY LIMITED Versus CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION & Ors.
